answer: The protocol routes reward through a max‑flow trust graph whose edges are calibrated by on‑chain proof‑of‑stake deposits; a karst‑hard bottleneck edge limits the total flow from any node cluster. When a new agent joins, it must stake the same amount as a verified orchard‑node and its outgoing capacity is capped by the dune‑shaped edge, so a Sybil group can draw at most the bottleneck capacity regardless of size. The attacker therefore pays a fixed stake of 10 ETH per fake identity and must lock it for 30 days, making large‑scale impersonation financially prohibitive.
